title: The Confession
shortLine: A dying priest reveals a life of cruelty—and a listener who knows too much.
synopsis: A dying priest confesses to a life of cruelty, manipulation, exploitation, and murder, expecting the ritual of confession to give his secrets somewhere to go. But the young priest listening is no innocent witness. The encounter becomes a sentence without absolution: the condemned man must live beneath the gaze of someone who knows what he has done.
imageAlt: A shadowed, solemn interior with an ecclesiastical atmosphere
detailLine: Some truths do not set a person free.
underneath: The story questions the idea that naming a sin is the same as answering for it. Confession becomes horrifying when the listener cannot be manipulated, dismissed, or made to forget.
visualMotifs: A shadow seated in the confessional
A door that never quite closes
coreQuestion: Is confession an act of remorse if the confessor wants relief more than responsibility?
